The test image shows a corn ear with dark green to gray-green mold growing between yellow kernels. This is a seed/ear disease. Top candidates based on mold color: **Trichoderma_Ear_Rot** and **Aspergillus_Ear_Rot**.

Let me view reference images, one per class across my top candidates first.
Trichoderma reference shows dark green mold on/between yellow kernels - very similar to the test image. Now let me check Aspergillus.
Aspergillus is more olive-green and powdery, covering kernels like dust. The test image has darker, more blue-green mold concentrated between kernels. Let me check the remaining ear diseases.
Fusarium shows white/pink mold - clearly different. Let me check Gibberella, Diplodia, and other candidates.
Gibberella shows pink/red mold at ear tip - clearly different. Let me check Diplodia and Common_Smut.
Diplodia shows grayish-brown mummified kernels - different. Let me check Common_Smut and Head_Smut.
Common Smut shows large white/silvery galls - completely different. Let me check Head_Smut.
Head Smut shows dark spore masses replacing the ear - different. Now let me use my last view to see a second Trichoderma reference to confirm.

This second Trichoderma reference shows the dark green conidia on husk leaves, consistent with the disease description.

**Analysis summary:**

- **Test image**: Corn ear with dark blue-green to gray-green mold growing extensively between and around yellow kernels. Kernels still visible but mold fills the spaces between them.
- **Trichoderma_Ear_Rot** (ref 1): Very close match. Same dark green mold on and between yellow kernels, same color and pattern.
- **Aspergillus_Ear_Rot**: More olive-green, powdery, covers kernels like dust. Different texture and color.
- **Fusarium**: White/pink mold. No match.
- **Gibberella**: Red/pink mold at tip. No match.
- **Diplodia**: White mycelium, grayish-brown mummified. No match.
- **Common_Smut**: Large galls. No match.
- **Head_Smut**: Dark spore masses replacing ear. No match.

The dark blue-green mold between kernels in the test image is a strong visual match for Trichoderma_Ear_Rot, consistent with the KB description of "dark blue-green layers of conidia on and between kernels."
